title: The Alleged Spy Who Brought Down Nvidia's CEO
hook: A woman sat beside Jensen Huang at a dinner in Taipei. Eighteen months later, a secret US intelligence memo claimed she was working for China.
thumbnail_picture: Huge close view on the right of a composed woman about 40 with shoulder-length black hair and a dark business blazer at a candlelit restaurant table, half her face in deep shadow, one eye glancing sideways with a faint knowing smile, a man in rectangular glasses and a black leather jacket blurred beside her looking shocked, warm amber light, the left third of the frame empty dark background
description:
A dinner in Taipei. A woman few people had heard of. And, eighteen months later, a secret US intelligence memo alleging she was recruited by China's spy agency to get close to Nvidia's CEO, Jensen Huang.

This is the story of the boy who cleaned school bathrooms and built the world's most valuable chip company, the AI chips America would not let China buy, a Singapore company that bought billions of dollars of them, and the allegations that ended in his resignation.

Important: the spying claims in this video come from news reports about a US intelligence memo. They have not been proven in court. Megaspeed denies breaking any law, and Alice Huang has not publicly given her side.

Sources: reporting by The New York Times, Reuters, The Wall Street Journal, TechCrunch and The Information.
